baselines.name: cascast_nwp
baselines.license: NOASSERTION (no LICENSE file in upstream repo)
baselines.upstream_notes: Upstream is radar-only SEVIR 13-in/12-out at 384x384; this adapter adds NWP conditioning and adapts to 11-in/10-out.

baselines.name: convlstm
baselines.upstream_notes: The classic deep-learning baseline for radar nowcasting: the NWP fields are broadcast along the channel axis and concatenated to the radar history before the recurrent core. It is the reference point for 'how much does a modern architecture buy over a plain ConvLSTM'.

baselines.name: diffcast
baselines.license: GPL-3.0 (upstream; this adapter is an independent reimplementation)
baselines.upstream_notes: Upstream is radar-only 5-in/20-out at 128x128; this adapter adds an NWP conditioning path.

baselines.name: earthformer
baselines.upstream_notes: The space-time transformer baseline. The radar history and the NWP fields are embedded as 4x-downsampled patches and mixed by cuboid self-attention over the time and space axes.

baselines.name: furecast
baselines.upstream_notes: Upstream is polarimetric (ZH/ZDR/KDP); this adapter uses the CAPPI channel set with a CAPPI-level self-consistency penalty.

baselines.name: fusioncast
baselines.license: NOASSERTION (no LICENSE file in upstream repo)
baselines.upstream_notes: Upstream second modality is GNSS PWV (substituted here by NWP) and its loss function is withheld upstream.

baselines.name: metnet3
baselines.upstream_notes: Upstream targets 24 h / 2 min CONUS forecasts; this adapter adapts it to the 6-min / 10-frame regime with MaxViT blocks and lead-time conditioning.

baselines.name: mmf_rnn
baselines.upstream_notes: Upstream second modality is ground-station gauges, which this benchmark lacks; NWP substitutes for the gauge modality.

baselines.name: mocast
baselines.upstream_notes: Upstream uses input T=5 / output P=20 on SEVIR; this adapter reimplements the paper description and adapts it to the 6-min / 10-frame regime with NWP conditioning.

baselines.name: physical_qpe
baselines.upstream_notes: Oracle upper bound is CSI@2.0 = 0.1653 (perfect QPE + no motion); analytical Z-R persistence floor is 0.0924. Trained with --loss balanced --qpe-single-frame so the score-aware objective supervises ONLY y_hist[:, -1], never a future frame. Evaluated by the standard scripts/evaluate.py, which stitches the full 301x301 grid.

baselines.name: physical_qpe_v2
baselines.upstream_notes: D3 paired ablation: use_gate=true/false must differ by ONLY the gate. Trained with --loss balanced --qpe-single-frame, 3 epochs, evaluated per epoch with the standard full-grid 301x301 Hann stitching. Reference: v1 ep00 CSI@2.0 = 0.1226 (section 4.19).

baselines.name: predrnn
baselines.upstream_notes: The stochastic video-prediction baseline adapted to nowcasting. The NWP fields enter through the channel axis of the encoder, and the spatio-temporal memory cell carries the uncertainty state across the recurrent steps.

baselines.name: pw_foucast
baselines.license: NOASSERTION (no LICENSE file in upstream repo)
baselines.upstream_notes: Upstream hardcodes 20 Pangu channels and a 5-in/20-out regime; this adapter adapts it to 27 NWP variables and 11-in/10-out.

baselines.name: pysteps_adv
baselines.upstream_notes: A semi-Lagrangian extrapolation baseline: the optical flow between the last two radar frames is estimated by finite differences and the last frame is advected forward, then converted to rainfall through the Z-R relation. It is the operational reference -- a forecast that does not learn anything must still be beaten. It ignores the NWP entirely, so it also bounds what the radar alone can do without any learning.

baselines.name: simvp_early_concat
baselines.upstream_notes: Ablation baseline: the NWP fields are broadcast along the channel axis and concatenated to the radar history, with no dedicated encoder and no fusion gate. It answers whether the naive way of adding NWP -- paste it onto the channels -- is already enough, which is the control the more elaborate fusion architectures have to beat.

baselines.name: simvp_radar_only
baselines.upstream_notes: Ablation baseline: the same SimVP core as simvp_v2, but with no NWP input at all. It is the structural counterpart of the --no-nwp ablation -- the ablation keeps the architecture and removes the information, this one removes both -- so the two together say how much of the gap is the network and how much is the fields.

baselines.name: simvp_v2
baselines.upstream_notes: The MLP-based video-prediction baseline, adapted to nowcasting. It is the cheapest of the multimodal baselines here, so it doubles as a control: if the NWP ablation moves it as much as it moves the heavy models, the effect is an artefact of the training budget rather than of the architecture.

baselines.name: simvp_v2_assimilated
baselines.upstream_notes: Route R2. The observed history rainfall is assimilated as an input channel; the lagged slots are filled by the model's own inversion, so the model degrades gracefully as the observation gets later. Compare within this family (lag 0 / 2 / 4 / 11), not against the radar baselines.

baselines.name: simvp_v2_hqma
baselines.upstream_notes: Hybrid Quantum Manifold Architecture. Shallow concatenation of the radar and the NWP channels (the part M1 proved worth keeping), a deep Koopman tendency read from the two NWP slices and applied per forecast frame, and a hierarchical projection head that predicts a nested distribution over the rain bins rather than a single regressed number. The head exists because the measured frequency bias of every model trained with a single-channel head was 0.08-0.33 -- they predicted between two and a third of the rain that fell. Train it with --loss hierarchical so the exceedance probabilities are supervised; with --loss standard the head's probabilities are unused and the head contributes little. Compare against simvp_v2 (backbone), simvp_v2_nwp_concat (M1) and simvp_v2_quantum (M4).

baselines.name: simvp_v2_lagrangian
baselines.upstream_notes: Route R4. The forecast is a gated blend of a semi-Lagrangian advection of the inverted rainfall and a learned source/sink residual. Compare the three ablation arms with each other before comparing with the baselines, and read the gate weight and the mass ratio alongside the scores.

baselines.name: simvp_v2_nwp_concat
baselines.upstream_notes: Ablation row M1 of the NWP-injection study: the NWP forecast slice is pasted onto the radar history on the input channels, so the first convolution sees 37 of them, and the backbone is SimVP-v2's unchanged. It is the control that answers 'does merely having the NWP help?', against which the cross-attention row and the tendency-difference row are read.

baselines.name: simvp_v2_nwp_delta
baselines.upstream_notes: Ablation row M3 of the NWP-injection study: the model is given the difference between the NWP's forecast hour and its analysis hour, and nothing else of the NWP. It is the control that answers 'is the tendency the useful part of the NWP, or is it the state?', because the difference is exactly the tendency without any Koopman or quantum-inspired machinery to extract it.

baselines.name: simvp_v2_nwp_xattn
baselines.upstream_notes: Ablation row M2 of the NWP-injection study: the NWP is encoded into a feature map and the radar latent queries it through an ordinary multi-head spatial cross-attention (common.SpatialCrossAttention), with no Koopman or quantum-inspired machinery anywhere. It is the control that answers 'would any competent conventional fusion of the NWP have done as well as the tendency coupler?', and it is deliberately a strong row rather than a straw man.

baselines.name: simvp_v2_qpe_guided
baselines.upstream_notes: Route R1. The archive's radar and rainfall series share their timestamps, so the eleven history instants have an observed rainfall each, with no displacement error between the radar and the truth. This model uses that: an inversion branch is supervised directly against the observed history rainfall, and the forecast branch works in the space of the inverted rainfall. The two share one rainfall head, so the zero-displacement supervision anchors the forecast. At inference the model consumes exactly what the baselines consume -- the training objective supplies the observed history.

baselines.name: simvp_v2_quantum
baselines.upstream_notes: The reference integration of the quantum-inspired NWP tendency coupler (QuantumStateProjector + KoopmanUnitaryFlow + FiLM). It exists to show that the coupling is a plug-in: the backbone, the head and the loss are SimVP-v2's, and the coupler is one line. Compare against simvp_v2 to see what the coupling buys.
